deck.topic: Texas option period: how buyers burn their walk-away window
deck.hook: You lose 3 of your 7 walk away days.

points.title: You Are Buying Time
body: The option fee is not a deposit. It buys you the right to walk for any reason at all.
It is small money for the strongest position you will have in the whole deal.

points.title: Where Your 3 Days Go
body: The clock counts weekends and holidays. It does not pause because it is Sunday.
A good inspector is booked two or three days out. So 3 of your 7 days are gone before anyone steps inside the house.
points.loop: The report is not the finish line.

points.title: Nobody Owes You Repairs
body: A seller can read your inspection report and do absolutely nothing. That is allowed.
The report is information. It is not a to do list they signed up for.
points.loop: How you ask changes the answer.

points.title: Ask For Money Instead
body: A seller under deadline pressure hires the cheapest guy who can come Thursday.
Ask for a credit or a price cut and you pick your own contractor after closing.
points.loop: There is a wrong week for that.

points.title: Verbal Means Nothing
body: Telling your agent you are out is not termination. Notice has to be delivered in writing before the deadline.
Miss it by one hour and you own the contract, with your earnest money sitting on the table.
points.loop: Day one decides most of this.

linkedinCaption:
The Texas option period is the strongest position a buyer will hold in the entire transaction, and it gets wasted more often than not.

A few things worth understanding before you sign. The option fee is not a deposit. It buys the unconditional right to terminate. The clock runs on calendar days, including Sunday, and a good inspector is usually booked two or three days out. That alone can consume half a seven day window.

A seller is also free to read the report and do nothing. Asking for a credit instead of repairs lets you choose the contractor later. And termination must be in writing, delivered before the deadline. Verbal notice to your agent is not termination.

Agents: how many option days are you writing right now, and why?
